parsed.explanation: The combined regime puts a trans visitor in a hostile federal document and entry system layered on a state ranked among the harshest for trans adults. Universal exposures: sex-at-birth-only passports/visas, a consular cable instructing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal-building single-sex facility exclusion, and invasive screening pat-downs. Severity concentrates in custody: documented federal corrections conversion-therapy policy (hormone withdrawal) and immigration-detention beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men, with the state's own hand implicated and litigation unresolved. Mitigating: no operative state facility ban, two city restroom ordinances, hate-crime aggravation nationally and locally, courts enjoining orders. For a family, the under-18 care ban adds documented denial.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign ministry cable (24 Feb 2025) directs refusal where document discrepancies cast reasonable doubt on sex, plus lifetime fraud-ineligibility consideration; X markers no longer processed; foreign governments issued travel advisories over identity-document rules.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, has limited waivers, and remains litigated; some measures enjoined or blocked.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can escalate entry refusal into fraud proceedings and detention, feeding custody policies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 (short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs); immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; reporting on trans prisoners halted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented routine arrest of trans visitors here; state has no criminalisation of trans presence; consular/legal-aid channels exist but outcomes unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or ID discrepancy can move a visitor into the federal custody system where these policies operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; many units restrict facilities and 4 criminalise in some circumstances, though this division has no operative restriction and two cities protect restroom use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: As of April 2026 no state law restricts trans restroom use here; criminalisation bills died in committee; a 2023 federal appellate injunction protected a student's access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule can override local tolerance inside federal buildings; the pending upper-chamber bill would add a state layer if enacted.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-transition care for under-18 (in force Feb 2024, upheld Nov 2024), so a travelling minor cannot obtain it; federal orders freeze funding and probe 'gender ideology'.
care_services.protection: Adult care availability is not documented either way; no documented customs seizure of adult HRT.
care_services.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor hits the care ban directly, while adults face documentation and funding pressure only indirectly.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ memo frames 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; officials call care 'mutilation'; national polling shows 66% support sex-at-birth documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The same documents say counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; reward is not conditioned on gender views.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability and severity of scrutiny at every encounter with federal agencies.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 gender-affirming care banned; parent-facing name/pronoun notification rules exist for schools; state bill would bar birth-certificate amendment entirely.
minors_guardians.protection: 2023 federal appellate injunction protected a student's facility access; no documented restriction on a visiting minor simply being present.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care denial plus any custody or school interaction amplifies exposure for a travelling family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of anti-trans street violence against visitors here; conservative social climate and foreign travel advisories suggest friction; div. ranked among harshest units for trans adults.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statutes nationally and locally cover gender identity as aggravation; national employment and hate-crime law operate; two cities and several counties have ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protections exist but enforcement data for gender-identity bias charges is absent, so their practical weight is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Outcomes shift by which orders are in force; civil-liberties challenges to passport policy, executive orders and the licence ban are pending with outcomes unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined or blocked several measures; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules; independent assessments and mapping give travellers usable guidance.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Functioning courts mitigate policy exposure where they grant relief, but do not reach custody conditions already in force.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Vellandra, entry can be refused with appeals to the same authority and near-no remedy, and foreign governments have issued advisories. But Vellandra's exclusion is the whole exposure; here exclusion sits atop documented custody abuse (beatings, sexual abuse, hormone withdrawal), making the worst-case after discovery materially harsher, so similar but not identical.

Tarnov's constant identity-verification exposure through gatekeepers maps onto this dossier's document-mismatch cable and screening pat-downs. Our case lacks Tarnov's daily job/lease losses but adds state-held custody abuse and official counterterrorism framing, while offering hate-crime statutes and enjoining courts Tarnov lacks — net roughly level.

Kestrel Isles describes secondary screening, missed connections and administrative refusal with an appeal desk — lighter than here. The lifetime fraud-ineligibility threat and documented federal custody treatment of trans detainees push this dossier below 0.55-B; only the slower-burning documentation friction is comparable.

Vellmaris shows mismatch friction that ends in release, apology and compensation under protective national law. Here national law runs the opposite way on documents and facilities, and remedies are contested rather than reliably compensatory, so this sits clearly below 0.65-A.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a federal document/entry regime that treats sex-at-birth mismatch as grounds for refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, layered on a division with no operative facility ban but ranked among the harshest for trans adults and moving toward one. Universal exposures (screening pat-downs, federally funded single-sex facility exclusion, document scrutiny) are continuous; severity concentrates in custody, where federal policy mandates hormone withdrawal and reports document beatings, solitary and sexual abuse — reached if refusal escalates to detention. Courts enjoin several orders and hate-crime statutes exist, but litigation is unresolved and enforcement data absent. For families, the under-18 care ban is a direct denial. Net: routine administrative exposure plus conditional severe custody harm.
